soundness_flags.label: Theorem 4 (global inversion)
soundness_flags.one_line: The two advertised coverage inequalities follow immediately from simultaneous coverage of q by R_n and the definitions of C_n and H_n; promote a nontrivial computational/radius result or demote these inclusions to a corollary.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 238(2), 2024; claim comparison corroborated against arXiv:2012.02390v2 because the publisher full text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.locator: Journal landing metadata; corroborating preprint pp. 24-26, Assumption 5, Lemma 3, and footnote 29
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 5 is full support among compliers; footnote 29 says that without it the bounding quantiles must be generalized and relevant extrema may fail to be jointly attainable by one rank-similar process.
The paper gives asymptotic theory for compact convex identification regions represented as transformations of Aumann expectations.
The paper constructs estimators, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-minimizer identified sets.
The paper constructs random sets covering identified minimizer sets or their known-function images, including uniform asymptotic validity under conditions.
With Gaussian limits, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary-bootstrap consistency; the alternative scheme requires the relevant directional derivative.
Calibrated projection provides uniformly valid intervals for components and smooth functions in moment-(in)equality models through repeated feasibility checks.
The paper develops sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds and studies normal and bootstrap inference for them.
The paper gives a closed-form categorical-IV compatibility characterization and finite-sample simultaneous confidence intervals for linear counterfactual functionals.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Demote the tautological coverage inclusions in Theorem 4 to a corollary and make its theorem target an explicit finite algorithm for Hausdorff radii, with input size and complexity/termination bounds over the path systems.

State a nontrivial finite-sample optimality or unavoidable-conservatism comparison for the inversion radius, tied to the path-drop lower-bound family, rather than presenting image coverage as the contribution.
Correct the Marx bibliography metadata from Journal of Econometrics 240 to the verified Journal of Econometrics 238(2), 105561, and retain the Proposition 5/footnote 29 anchor.

recommended_next_step: Revise Theorem 4 into a substantive computability or radius theorem; the path-union, continuity, and path-drop kernel otherwise clears field-tier novelty review.
